artboards.role: Forno Rosso pizzeria marketing home page: header/nav, hero, delivery promo banner, featured (Chef Recommendations) menu grid, brand-story section, footer. The linked node is a single FRAME, not a CANVAS of several artboards, so there is only one screen to review. This story's scope is the featured-menu grid (featured-section / featured-grid); the rest of the page is mapped for continuity with MANOJ-ADMIN-PROJECT-STORY-004, which already shipped the header.

open_questions.topic: FeaturedGrid has no responsive design below 1440px
open_questions.detail: The frame fixes featured-grid (6:59) at exactly 4 columns x 302px cards for a 1440px canvas; no tablet or mobile column count is drawn anywhere. This story is specifically about shipping this grid, so the gap is now directly in scope (STORY-004 deferred the equivalent question for the header).
open_questions.arc_assumption: Reuse the app's existing useIsMobileViewport hook/pattern (src/features/site/useIsMobileViewport.ts, 640px breakpoint) and lay the grid out with CSS grid auto-fit, collapsing from 4 columns at desktop widths to 2 columns on tablet and 1 column at/below 640px, rather than shipping a fixed 1280px-wide grid that would overflow on smaller viewports.

options.label: Responsive grid: 4 cols desktop, 2 cols tablet, 1 col mobile (≤640px) — extrapolated from the app's existing mobile breakpoint, not drawn in the frame
Ship the grid fixed at the designed 1280px/4-column layout only, matching the frame pixel-for-pixel with no reflow below it

open_questions.topic: Two menu card titles are truncated or near the edge of the 302px card width
open_questions.detail: 'Funghi Selvatici & Tartufo' (6:77) renders as 'Funghi Selvatici &...' in the PNG, and 'Prosciutto Crudo e Rucola' (6:101) is close to the same limit — the design does not show what a graceful 2-line wrap or smaller font-size fallback should look like.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Let MenuItemCard's title wrap to 2 lines instead of truncating, since clipping a dish name mid-word is a worse outcome for a menu than a slightly taller title block.

options.label: Wrap the title to 2 lines and let that row grow — a visible departure from the single-line PNG for long names
Keep the single-line ellipsis truncation exactly as rendered (6:77 crops to 'Funghi Selvatici &...')
Auto-shrink the title font-size until it fits one line, keeping the row height fixed

open_questions.topic: Whether hero CTAs and card 'Add to Order' buttons share one Button component
open_questions.detail: Hero has a primary red-fill button with a trailing arrow icon and an outline button with no icon; each MenuItemCard has a dark-fill button with a leading plus icon. All three share size, radius (8px), and type style but differ in fill/border/icon placement.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Model all three as one shared Button component with variant ('primary' | 'outline' | 'dark') and icon/iconPosition props, instead of near-duplicate components. Carried over from STORY-004's mapping of the same frame.

open_questions.topic: Whether featured-section and story-section headings share one SectionHeading component
open_questions.detail: featured-section uses a brand-red uppercase eyebrow with a short rule under the title; story-section uses a brand-green uppercase eyebrow with no rule. Layout (eyebrow above serif title) is otherwise identical.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Model both as one shared SectionHeading component with eyebrowTone ('accent' | 'brand') and showRule props. Carried over from STORY-004's mapping of the same frame.

open_questions.topic: MenuItemCard's internal proportions vary across instances despite equal outer card height
open_questions.detail: All 4 cards are 441px tall, but the Prosciutto card's description block is 84px vs 63px for the other three (6:103 vs 6:67/6:79/6:91), and its content wrapper (6:97) is 377px vs 356px — real menu copy will not always be this evenly sized.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Build MenuItemCard as a fixed-width, auto-height flex column (image, then a content block that grows with description length, then the Add to Order button) rather than a hard-coded 441px card height, so longer copy doesn't clip or force artificial truncation.

open_questions.topic: Header still has a designed 'Cart' affordance that isn't built
open_questions.detail: The frame shows both a plain 'Cart' nav link (6:18) and a separate cart icon button with a live-count badge (6:22) in the header. STORY-004 shipped SiteHeader with only Home/Our Menu (matching the two routes that exist today) and no CartButton at all.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Leave this gap for whichever story adds a cart/checkout flow: it needs a /cart route before the NavLink instance and CartButton (icon + count prop) can be wired in. Not part of this story's scope, noted here only because the featured-grid's 'Add to Order' buttons imply a cart will exist soon.

open_questions.topic: Hero eyebrow badge's icon layer is misnamed relative to its glyph
open_questions.detail: Node 6:679 is named 'fire-extinguisher' but the rendered PNG shows a flame glyph, and 'Authentic Neapolitan Woodfired' pairs naturally with fire/flame, not an extinguisher.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Render lucide's 'flame' icon here rather than 'fire-extinguisher', treating the Figma layer name as a mislabeled instance swap rather than an intentional choice.

open_questions.topic: '900°F Stone Hearth Wood Oven' feature uses a compass icon
open_questions.detail: FeatureListItem icons are star (tomatoes), shield (mozzarella), and compass (wood oven, 6:595) — compass has no obvious semantic link to an oven or fire, unlike the other two pairings.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Render the icon exactly as designed (lucide 'compass') rather than substituting a flame/oven icon; unlike hero-badge-icon-name this isn't an obvious mislabel, just an unusual pairing, so the frame is trusted as authoritative.

open_questions.topic: No icon assets are exported for the ~11 vector icons in this frame
open_questions.detail: figma-assets.json only lists photographic fills (hero, 4 menu cards, 2 story photos); fire-extinguisher, arrow-right, truck, plus, star, shield, compass, instagram, facebook, twitter and shopping-cart are all vector node names that match lucide-react icon ids exactly.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Introduce lucide-react as the icon source and wrap it in a local Icon(name) component rather than hand-authoring 11 new SVGs, since the naming match is too exact to be coincidental.

open_questions.topic: Delivery time shown twice with different values
open_questions.detail: Header shows 'Estimated delivery: 30 mins' (6:21) while the delivery banner states 'Average ETA: 25 - 35 Min' (6:50). These may be an intentional live-order-estimate vs. site-wide-average split, or just inconsistent placeholder copy.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Implement both strings literally as authored, as two independent copy sources with no shared data binding, and flag the discrepancy for content review. Carried over from STORY-004's mapping of the same frame.

open_questions.topic: Supplied component catalogue said greenfield, but the repo already has site components from STORY-004
open_questions.detail: The task prompt states 'no existing UI components in this project', but src/features/site already contains SiteHeader, PrimaryNav, NavLink, BrandLogo, and DeliveryIndicator, built for MANOJ-ADMIN-PROJECT-STORY-004.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Follow the stated catalogue literally: every node in component_map above is marked status: proposed_new, with no exceptions, since the catalogue says no UI components exist yet. Where matching code already lives in src/features/site (SiteHeader, PrimaryNav, NavLink, BrandLogo, DeliveryIndicator, from STORY-004), that is called out in the relevant entry's notes so an implementer reuses/extends it instead of duplicating it — but status itself is not overridden.
